Presets · round 6

Round 6: the chain screen made vertical, after the video mockup’s one sheet — nine shapes in the new ★ Vertical tab, seven split layouts in ★ Split, and how the sheet handles a PDF, a failure and a slow step. Round 5 below it, unchanged.

The chain screen (your idea: the chain stays on top, each step opens below it), taken further: seven ways to handle a long chain, eight different concepts for the screen itself, and eleven edge cases. Example: photo.png → WebP 80 → 1920 wide → Sharpen → …, saved as blog.

Questions for you

  1. Vertical (tab ★ Vertical): S1–S9? I pick S1, the sheet: every operation always a row, a chain is which rows are set. It is the one that changes the model — no adding, no order, no long chains — and S3’s “worth” column or S6’s switches could join it.
  2. Split (tab ★ Split): P1–P7, or none? P1 (the sheet left, the lit row’s controls right) is the one I’d pair with S1.
  3. If S1: does Done’s More operations open the sheet (S1), or is the sheet under Done itself (S4)?
  4. Long chains (tab ★ Long chains): L1–L7? I pick L3, the window that follows you.
  5. The chain screen (tab ★ Chain concepts): V1 (yours) still, or one of the new concepts C1–C8? I still pick V1 — but C1 (sizes per step) and C5 (switch a step off) do things V1 can’t; either could be folded into it.
  6. Edge cases (tab ★ Edge cases): is the proposed behaviour right for each of E1–E11?
  7. Each step runs as soon as you confirm it, so the result line is always real. Or build the whole chain first and run once at the end?
  8. esc ends the chain and goes back to Done; x on a box removes that step. OK?
  9. The chain keeps one file: each step replaces what the chain wrote before. OK?
  10. Done: D1–D6? I pick D1.
  11. New words, to approve: “More operations”, “Save as preset”, “x remove”, “↵ change”, “not for a PDF”, “can’t follow a PDF”, “found no subject”, “↵ try again”, “1 failed”, “add · 41 MB”, “Update blog”, “Save as new”, and C7’s whole sentence if picked.

WHAT A PRESET CAN HOLD

Every action Forge has today, from src/core/actions. A step keeps its answers as a rule that fits any file of its kind.

Stepswhat you do to a file, in order: Convert to WebP 80, then Resize to 1920 wide. Two or more is what we called a pipeline — the inside word; screens only say “step”.Presetsteps you kept, under a name, with where to save. One step is enough.
StepWorks onWhat the preset keepsNotes
Convertimages, PDFs, Wordthe format and its quality; for a PDF, the pages (all · first) and dpitargets still come from each file (invariant 2)
Compressimages, PDFsby quality, or to a target size (“under 500 KB”)a target size suits presets best
Resizeimagesa width, a height or a % — chosen when saving“longest side” missing
Trim edgesimageson
Crop to shapeimagesthe shape, e.g. 16:9a hand-placed crop is per photo; the preset places it as Forge does unplaced
Sharpen · Boost resolutionimageson · 2× 3× 4×need Boost installed
Remove backgroundimagesonmacOS, needs the extension
RotatePDFs90° right · 180° · 90° left, all pages
SplitPDFsevery page · every N pages“at points I choose” is per document
Extract · Delete · MergePDFs, several files—page numbers are per document; merge is many-in. Later
Setting of the presetValues
nameletters, digits, dashes — so /blog and --preset blog work
toa folder · Ask each time · Same location
filesame name · name-preset (photo-blog.webp)
metadataremoved (default) · kept — --keep-metadata exists

Not steps: colour (makes a palette, not a file); a locked PDF’s password (asked each time, never stored).
